newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus sues French TV channels over adverts.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus sues French TV channels over adverts.

text.p: French pay television group Canal Plus said it was suing the French terrestrial television channels and their media-selling units over their refusal to accept an advert promoting Canal Plus last April.

Canal Plus said in a statement late on Monday that private channels TF1 and M6 and public channels France 2 and France 3 had "seriously abused their position to the detriment of the principles of freedom of commerce and competition".

"The refusal by TF1, France 2, France 3 and M6 to accept this advertising campaign deprives Canal Plus of access to practically all national terrestrial television screens and constitutes a violation of freedom of expression and plurality of information," it said.

Canal Plus said it had filed a suit with the Paris commercial court against the television companies and had asked the court to make the television companies broadcast the advertising spots in September.
A Canal Plus spokeswoman said the court was due to consider the case on August 30.

TPS, the digital satellite television service operated by TF1 which rivals Canal Plus's Canalsatellite, has taken Canal Plus to the competition court, saying the pay television group was using its dominant position to prevent competitors from buying film rights, Le Monde newspaper reported on Monday.
TPS and Canal Plus, when contacted by Reuters, declined to comment.
TPS carries three specialist film channels, including pay-per-view channel Multivision.

Before cable and satellite television services became widely available in France -- the digital satellite services date only from the beginning of this year -- Canal Plus had a monopoly of the French pay television market.
